edges.description: A conduction system built with too few cells has no reserve against the postnatal attrition of those cells.
High-grade block with an inadequate escape rate causes transient cerebral hypoperfusion.

Complete atrioventricular block without adequate escape rhythm causes syncope and can cause sudden death; the intermediate steps are bradycardia and haemodynamic collapse or secondary ventricular arrhythmia.
Ectopic BMP10 is not merely correlated with the trabecular phenotype; it is required for a major part of it.
The noncompacted, fibrotic ventricle remodels over years into a dilated and functionally impaired chamber.
The remodelled, fibrotic ventricle of the myopathic arm becomes an arrhythmic substrate.
Atrial remodelling accompanying the myopathic arm predisposes to atrial arrhythmia.
Maternal age shifts the probability that the septal defect occurs at a given genotype; the mechanism linking the two is not established.
